fossil-fuels-power-plant.alt: A coal-fired power plant drawn as connected boxes. Coal goes into the boiler, which heats water into steam and sends smoke and carbon dioxide up a stack. Steam spins the turbine, whose shaft turns the generator, which sends electricity out. Used steam goes to the condenser, where cooling water from a river or cooling tower turns it back to water, which returns to the boiler; the cooling water leaves warmer as waste heat. A banner says about one third of the fuel's energy leaves as electricity and about two thirds is lost as heat.
